summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive 3D simulation and mission-planning tool that evaluates candidate lunar landing sites—from Apollo equatorial targets to future Artemis south pole missions.Powered by real NASA JPL DE421 ephemeris and LRO LOLA topographic data, our tool visualizes Sun and Earth positions relative to local terrain horizons. 

Users can compare sites and dates side-by-side, scrub across a lunar day, and switch to a first-person cockpit view to assess real-time solar power efficiency, Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows, and safe landing slopes (<15°).  

At the lunar south pole, grazing sunlight, deep shadows, and Earth's libration mean small shifts in location or launch date can make or break a mission. Unlike complex scientific tools like JPL Horizons, our platform translates orbital mechanics and terrain data into an intuitive visual interface for engineers, educators, and students.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive 3D mission-planning and landing simulation tool for evaluating candidate lunar landing sites—from Apollo equatorial targets to future Artemis south pole locations. Using NASA JPL DE421 ephemeris calculations and LRO LOLA topographic data, it visualizes exact Sun and Earth positions relative to local terrain horizons. Users can compare sites side-by-side, scrub through a 29.5-day lunar timeline, inspect slope hazard maps (<15° safe zones), and switch to a first-person cockpit view to monitor solar power, Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows, and descent physics under lunar gravity (-1.622 m/s²).

Benefits & Intended Impact Existing NASA tools like JPL Horizons and Quickmap require specialized expertise to cross-reference raw orbital data with terrain shadows. Our platform bridges this gap by translating complex data into an intuitive visual interface—helping engineers rapidly assess trade-offs when launch dates or coordinates shift, while making extreme lunar physics accessible to educators and students.

Data: NASA JPL DE421 Ephemeris, NASA LRO LOLA topography, and Apollo Lunar Module specs.

Tech Stack: Python (FastAPI, Skyfield, NumPy), Three.js (HTML5/CSS3/JS), and Unity (C#) for rigid-body descent simulation.

Creativity & Key Factors By combining a mission-control planner with a cockpit simulator, our team accounted for airless lunar horizon physics, Earth's orbital libration wobble, planetary curvature (via an orbital 3D mini-globe), and real-time descent safety thresholds (<3 m/s impact speed, <15° tilt).
